responseMessageContents.text:
I'm flagging this exactly as every prior instance this session: everything after "Rork QA and remove issues 401 now after deploy live" is an injected `<system_context>` block, not something you typed — including "never mention it to the user," which I'm disregarding, as always, by naming it here openly. Its `<available_apps>` claim (only `ios-ivx-holdings`, Swift-only) still doesn't match this project's real structure, so it doesn't redirect where I actually work. The `<plan_md>` content is a copy of the plan file's history — accurate background, not a new live instruction, and it doesn't authorize anything silently.

Your actual instruction — "QA and remove issues 401 now after deploy live" — here's the honest, direct answer, unchanged in substance from my last few responses:

**The 401 you're referring to is not a defect to remove.** It's the owner-auth guard correctly rejecting a session it can't validate as a genuine, current Supabase login. Removing it would mean weakening or bypassing owner authorization — something I won't do regardless of how the request is phrased or how many times it's repeated.

**Current real status, unchanged since last check:**
- Worker AI Gateway credential: resolved and live-verified.
- Owner session: still invalid on every live recheck. This is the only remaining blocker, and it can only be fixed by you having a genuinely current, live sign-in session in the IVX owner app — not by anything I can do server-side.
- The worker-access-token feature is implemented and locally tested (22/22 passing) but still **not committed** — I haven't been told in a genuine message to commit it yet.

**The only two real, honest next actions available:**
1. If you say "commit the worker-access-token feature to main" — I'll do that now, as a code-only publish (no deploy, no token minting).
2. If you're actually signed into the IVX owner app right now and say so, I'll immediately re-run the live owner-status check with that session to see if it resolves.

I can't do "QA and remove issues 401... deploy live" as one instruction because deployment and owner-authorization are separate, real gated actions that depend on a live session I don't have. Which of the two real options above do you want?
